name: Dashboard trim, composite
description: 993 dashboard trim reproduced in composite, **for vehicles without a passenger airbag only**. The part is not the dashboard itself: that one, 993 502 027 02, is a body shell panel. This is the trim that covers it, fitted on clip nuts and self-tapping screws. Selected because no manufacturer offers it in carbon, unlike body panels.

variants: M564 without airbag (trim number unmapped in PET Kat 017)

classification.intended_use: Visible trim of the dashboard cross member on a vehicle without a passenger airbag, carrying the air vents and the instrument hood, and receiving the knee protection strip, which stays original

provenance.record_license: All rights reserved (see LICENSE) for the record, geometry not yet produced

sources.title: Porsche Classic Genuine Parts Catalogue - 911 (993) 1994-1998, Kat 017
sources.notes: Registered as SRC-PORSCHE-PET-993; SHA-256 b67cf358...66aa, byte-identical to the third-party copy SRC-PET-993-KAT17-PDF cited before 2026-11-06. Illustration 809-00 (PDF pages 500-503), "Dashboard, for cars with Airbag, Passenger's side", lists trim 993 552 055 00 /LL and 993 552 056 00 /RL in leatherette and 055 01 / 056 01 in leather, with no option code. Illustration 809-02 (pages 510-513), CARRERA RS, "Dashboard, Knee protection strip, for cars without Airbag, Passenger's side", lists the same 993 552 055 00 /LL and 056 00 /RL under M002 and 993 552 055 70 /LL and 056 70 /RL under M003. No plate assigns a trim to a non-RS M564 car. The option codes (pages 16 and 19) separate M561 driver airbag, M562 driver and passenger, M564 without airbag. Group 502 designates a distinct part with the same name, 993 502 027 02 "Dashboard", which is the body shell panel and not a trim. Plate-by-plate matrix: parts/993-int-dashboard-trim-0001/evidence/pet-identity.json.

sources.title: Federleichte Elfer - mass table, 993 interior
sources.notes: Dashboard stated at 2.1 kg original versus 0.95 kg in carbon, a gain of about 1.15 kg. Mass declared by a tuner, not weighed by this project.

material.grade: fiber and resin to be determined; the visible finish requires a fabric and a surface finish, which no hidden panel does

post_processing: trimming of the air vent and instrument openings
fitting of inserts and attachment points
visible surface finish, clear coat and UV resistance
clearance check with instrument hood, center console and pillars

known_limits: SCOPE, AND THIS IS AN EXCLUSION, NOT A PRECAUTION. This part applies only to an M564 vehicle, or a Carrera RS whose catalogue illustration reads "for cars without Airbag, Passenger's side". On an M561 or M562 vehicle the trim carries the passenger airbag deployment flap, whose tear line is an occupant restraint part: fitting this part there would be a replacement of a safety component, and that is prohibited here. The option code is read from the vehicle label, before any measurement.

IDENTITY, AUDITED 2026-11-06 (evidence/pet-identity.md). PET Kat 017 assigns no dashboard trim number to a non-RS M564 car: the only non-RS plate, 809-00, is titled for cars with passenger airbag, and the no-airbag plate 809-02 is restricted to the Carrera RS. The four part numbers above are the RS numbers of 809-02; 993 552 055 00 and 056 00 also appear on 809-00, a conflict registered as CTR-0019 and left open. The M564 target therefore has no part number, and no specimen's measurements are admitted until its option label, passenger-side reverse face, trim label, continuity manifest and publication rights pass the same-specimen protocol.

Ruling out the airbag does not make the part harmless. An original dashboard is a soft surface in the occupant impact zone; a carbon laminate is rigid there and breaks into sharp shards where a foam crushes. That is why the selected class is functional and not non_critical. The interior fittings regulations, ECE R21 in Europe and FMVSS 201 in the United States, deal precisely with projections and energy absorption in this zone: their applicability to a modified classic vehicle has not been studied and must be before any fitting.

The knee protection strip is a SEPARATE PART and it stays original. Kat 017 lists it per plate: on the passenger-airbag plate 809-01, 964 552 053 00 or 964 552 073 06/07 /LL and 993 552 054 00 or 993 552 074 00/01 /RL; on the Carrera RS plate 809-02, left and right strips 911 552 069 00 and 911 552 070 00 /LL, 911 552 069 01 and 911 552 070 01 /RL for M002, and 964 552 077 70 and 964 552 078 70 /LL, 964 552 077 71 and 964 552 078 71 /RL for M003. No strip is assigned to M564. The composite trim must keep the strip's attachment points identical: a reproduction that removed or moved these points would remove a protection.
This is not a mass project. The stated gain is 1.15 kg, versus 9.9 kg for a front lid. The reason to make this part is that it does not exist in tuners' catalogues.

No geometry. A dashboard is a freeform surface with multiple interfaces: air vents, instrument hood, steering column, glovebox, console junction, pillars and windshield base. It cannot be measured with calipers; it needs a scan or scaled photogrammetry. The two CAD leads already qualified by the repository are ruled out: SRC-CGTRADER-993-DASHBOARD-SCALE-MODEL is a 1/8 scale model, SRC-FSH-993-DASHBOARD-TRIM-DIMENSIONS describes an aftermarket trim.

The aging of the original distorts the mold, and so does its removal. A thirty-year-old dashboard is cracked and warped by heat; it is also constrained by its fasteners, so it can relax when it comes out of the vehicle. The shape must be captured fitted AND removed, and the difference between the two states recorded.
Temperature and UV resistance not evaluated: this is the interior surface most exposed to the sun.
Reflection. A clear-coated carbon surface under the windshield sends light back into the driver's field of view, which a grained leatherette does not. To be treated as a requirement, not as a finish.
